hero.intro_html: The latest weekly conditions snapshot, the plot's dryness/water-loss maps from the historical analysis, and structural-break detection over the raw (uncomposited) NDVI series. None of these are finished alert products - the numbers below are published by hand whenever publish_site.py is re-run after a fresh local pass, not fetched live from the backend.

recent.title: Current conditions
recent.lede: Last ~2 months of Sentinel-2 data at weekly cadence, condensed into one composite: current NDVI/NDWI/NDMI plus a "% of the plot below the dry threshold" figure.
recent.quicklooks_lede: NDVI/NDWI/NDMI for the most recent usable weekly composite.

dryness.title: Where the plot loses water most
dryness.lede: Per-pixel dryness frequency (% of months below threshold) and deficit magnitude (how badly, on the months it was dry) - the frequency map complements the magnitude map: a sector can be dry often but mildly, or rarely but severely.
dryness.freq_desc: % of valid months each pixel was classified "dry".
dryness.ndwi_map_desc: Frequency + average deficit magnitude, side by side.
dryness.ndmi_map_desc: Same analysis, narrow-NIR index - compare against the NDWI version.

alerts.title: Vegetation break alerts
alerts.lede: A separate branch from the moisture monitoring above: every available raw Sentinel-2 scene over a chosen bounding box (no compositing), deseasonalized against a fixed harmonic model of the normal Central-European vegetation year (so ordinary spring green-up and autumn senescence aren't mistaken for a break) and searched for changepoints in what's left with ruptures' PELT - the same conceptual approach BFAST (Verbesselt et al.) is built on, via GPU-free, pip-installable libraries. Treat detected breaks as candidates worth a field check, not confirmed events or calibrated alerts.
alerts.table_lede: Each row is one candidate changepoint in the deseasonalized trend: the fitted trend level in the ~3 months before vs. after, and the resulting delta.
alerts.note_html: BFAST-style, not the literal BFAST/R package. Bounding box, lookback window, and penalty scale are all set in config.py (ALERT_BBOX, ALERT_YEARS, BFAST_PENALTY_SCALE). Natural next step (see README): turn the recent-conditions feed into a scheduled job that persists each run and diffs against the previous one to generate real alerts.

js.recent_error: Could not load the latest summary (data/drought_summary_latest.json) - run publish_site.py after the next drought_monitor_recent.py pass.
js.alert_error: Could not load alert_breaks.json - run bfast_alert.py then publish_site.py.
js.no_breaks: No structural breaks detected in this window.
js.chart_alt: Raw NDVI scatter, fitted trend, and detected breaks - {label}
